name: Maya Okafor
headline: Machine learning engineer, search and recommendation systems
summary: Machine learning engineer with 6 years building search and recommendation systems, after 4 years as a data analyst in retail. Leads ranking at a grocery marketplace and maintains an open-source evaluation toolkit that 300+ teams use.

claims.text: Replaced keyword search with hybrid retrieval and a learned reranker across 1.2M products; zero-result searches fell from 9% to 2%.

evidence.label: search conversion, A/B test over 6 weeks
evidence.source: Experiment report EXP-212, Basket analytics, Jun 2024

claims.text: Ranked replacements for out-of-stock items using basket context; shoppers now accept the first suggestion most of the time.
Moved the reranker to a distilled model with cached product embeddings, so results arrive before the shopper finishes typing.

evidence.label: 95th-percentile latency
evidence.source: Search service latency dashboard, Oct 2026; 420 ms from the Mar 2025 baseline report

claims.text: Every ranking change runs against 3,000 judged queries before release, and regressions block the merge.

evidence.label: judged queries per release
evidence.source: eval/judged_queries.jsonl in the search repo, row count

claims.text: Toolkit for judging and comparing search rankings without a live experiment, used by 300+ teams.
Built-in statistics that show when an LLM judge can stand in for human labels, validated on 5 public datasets.

sections.title: Previous roles

claims.text: Built semantic search over 40M de-identified notes for research teams, with access controls per study and an audit log for every query.

evidence.label: nDCG@10, up from 0.62
evidence.source: Lumen search evaluation, Jan 2023, 500 judged queries

claims.text: Let researchers describe a patient group in plain language and get a reviewable query, replacing a request queue handled by two analysts.

evidence.label: median wait for a cohort
evidence.source: Research-ops ticket export, 2021 vs. 2022; confirmed by Maya, Nov 2026

claims.text: Drift alerts and weekly accuracy reports for 12 production models, owned with the platform team.
Replaced a spreadsheet forecast with a gradient-boosted model per product family across 230 stores.

evidence.label: forecast error, down from 18%
evidence.source: Northwind forecast review deck, 2019; confirmed by Maya, Nov 2026

claims.text: Gave category managers a same-day view of promotion uplift, which had taken a week to compile by hand.

sections.note: Earlier: Teaching assistant, statistics, University of Porto (2015 – 2016).
